name: Goblet Cell Carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Goblet Cell Carcinoma

criteria.description: Presence of goblet cell morphology with mixed neuroendocrine and adenocarcinoma features on histology
Positive staining for neuroendocrine markers (chromogranin A, synaptophysin) and mucin markers (MUC2, MUC5AC)
Tumor primarily located in the appendix with possible local invasion
Symptoms consistent with appendiceal neoplasm such as right lower quadrant pain or acute appendicitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of goblet cell morphology with positive neuroendocrine and mucin immunohistochemical markers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires differentiation from typical carcinoid tumors and adenocarcinomas of the appendix.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Right lower quadrant abdominal pain mimicking acute appendicitis
searchTerms: right lower belly pain like appendicitis
pain in lower right abdomen mimicking appendicitis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable right lower quadrant abdominal mass
searchTerms: detectable lump in right lower abdomen
palpable mass in lower right belly
abdominal swelling felt on right side

common.symptomName: Altered bowel habits including diarrhea or constipation

occasional.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic disease or bleeding
searchTerms: low red blood cells from chronic illness
anemia caused by long-term disease or bleeding
reduced blood count due to chronic condition
flushing and diarrhea from hormone secretion
carcinoid symptoms like skin redness and loose stools
episodes of skin flushing and watery diarrhea

laboratory: Mild anemia on complete blood count
Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) in some cases
imaging: CT scan showing appendiceal mass with possible local invasion
Ultrasound demonstrating right lower quadrant mass or fluid collection
genetic: No consistent germline mutations identified; somatic mutations in KRAS and TP53 reported
other: Histopathology revealing mixed neuroendocrine and adenocarcinoma features
Immunohistochemical positivity for chromogranin A, synaptophysin, and mucin markers

distinguishingFeatures: Pure neuroendocrine differentiation without mucinous features
Predominantly glandular morphology without goblet cell features

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging right lower quadrant mass
Signs of bowel obstruction or perforation
Evidence of metastatic disease on imaging
references: Tang LH, Shia J, Soslow RA, et al. Pathologic classification and clinical behavior of goblet cell carcinoid tumors of the appendix. Am J Surg Pathol. 2008;32(10):1429-1443.

McCusker ME, Coté TR, Clegg LX, Sobin LH. Primary malignant neoplasms of the appendix: a population-based study from the Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results program, 1973-1998. Cancer. 2002;94(12):3307-3312.
